chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding a woman who vowed to perform Tawaf on four (crawling): She should perform one circuit (Usbu') for her hands and one circuit for her legs.

key_terms.أُسْبُوعاً: A circuit (seven days' worth of work or a specific measure)

ai.seo_question: How is a vow to perform Tawaf on all fours interpreted in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the vow of a woman who crawled on all fours by distinguishing between the movement of her hands and feet, ruling that one circuit for her hands and one for her legs constitute a complete Tawaf. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of *Tafsir al-Nadr* (interpretation of vows), where the literal action is weighed against the intent and physical reality, demonstrating the flexibility of Sharia in accommodating individual circumstances. The ruling underscores the importance of fulfilling vows with ease (*Yusr*) rather than undue hardship, a key theme in Shia legal theory.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said regarding a woman who vowed that she would be performing Tawaaf upon four (crawling). So heasws said: ‘She should perform Tawaaf of seven (circuits) for her hands, and seven (circuits) for her legs’.
en.sarwar: 18. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a woman who had made a vow to perform Tawaf on all-fours; legs and arms, said, ‘She must perform Tawaf once for her legs and once for her arms.’”
